facts.claim: Chinchilla is 70B parameters trained on 1.4T tokens and outperforms Gopher 280B, GPT-3 175B, Jurassic-1 178B and Megatron-Turing NLG 530B.
facts.note: Abstract and Section 1; compute-optimal ~20 tokens/parameter.

facts.claim: For compute-optimal training, model size and training tokens should scale equally; a doubling of parameters should be matched by a doubling of tokens.
facts.note: This is training-optimal, not inference-optimal.

facts.claim: phi-1 is 1.3B parameters, trained for 4 days on 8 A100s on 6B filtered web tokens plus 1B synthetic textbook tokens, and reaches 50.6% pass@1 on HumanEval and 55.5% on MBPP.
facts.note: Narrow code benchmark; synthetic data and HumanEval overlap must be considered.

facts.claim: phi-1.5 is 1.3B and performs comparably to models about 5x larger on natural-language tasks, while surpassing most non-frontier LLMs on grade-school math and basic coding.
facts.note: Vendor paper; 'comparable' is benchmark-dependent.

facts.claim: phi-3-mini is 3.8B, trained on 3.3T tokens, reaches 69% MMLU and 8.38 MT-Bench, and is positioned as rivaling Mixtral 8x7B and GPT-3.5 while fitting on a phone.
facts.note: Comparison targets are older/closed models; MMLU and MT-Bench are saturated and prompt-sensitive.

facts.claim: phi-4 is 14B and substantially surpasses its teacher (GPT-4) on STEM-focused QA; on the reported table it scores MMLU 84.8, GPQA 56.1, MATH 80.4, HumanEval 82.6, SimpleQA 3.0.
facts.note: It beats GPT-4o on MATH/GPQA but loses badly on SimpleQA (3.0 vs 39.4); this is the key 'small wins some, loses others' case.

facts.claim: TinyStories shows that models with ~10M parameters can generate coherent English when trained on a restricted synthetic story distribution, whereas ordinary 125M models rarely do.
facts.note: Does not imply general 10M language ability.

facts.claim: SmolLM2 is 1.7B, overtrained on ~11T tokens with a multi-stage mixture and new datasets FineMath, Stack-Edu and SmolTalk.
facts.note: A deliberate departure from Chinchilla-optimal for inference cost.

facts.claim: MobileLLM shows architecture matters at sub-billion scale: deep-and-thin, embedding sharing and GQA give 2.7%/4.3% accuracy gains over prior 125M/350M models; block-wise weight sharing adds further gains with little latency.
facts.note: Accuracy gains on zero-shot tasks; weight sharing trades compute for memory movement.

facts.claim: BitNet b1.58 uses ternary {-1,0,+1} weights and matches FP16/BF16 Transformers of the same size and training tokens on perplexity and end-task performance, with lower latency, memory, throughput and energy cost.
facts.note: Requires native low-bit kernels; do not expect speedups from a generic FP16 runtime.

facts.claim: BitNet b1.58 2B4T is a 2B native 1.58-bit model trained on 4T tokens; its card reports 0.4GB non-embedding memory, 29ms CPU TPOT, 0.028J estimated energy, and performance on par with similar-size full-precision models.
facts.note: The card itself warns generic transformers paths do not contain optimized kernels.

facts.claim: Distillation can beat supervised learning at equal compute up to a student-size-dependent threshold, but supervised learning always wins given enough student compute or tokens; if one student is trained and the teacher also must be trained, supervised learning is generally preferable.
facts.note: This is the strongest correction to 'distillation is always better'.

facts.claim: GKD trains the student on its own generated sequences with teacher feedback, addressing exposure bias from fixed teacher-forced sequences.
facts.note: The abstract does not claim a universal 2x; avoid inventing a number.

facts.claim: MiniLLM replaces forward KL with reverse KL and uses on-policy optimization; it scales from 120M to 13B students and improves calibration and long-text generation over sequence KD.
facts.note: Reverse KL is mode-seeking; it can reduce diversity.

facts.claim: Speculative decoding accelerates exact autoregressive sampling without changing the output distribution; the original work reports 2x-3x on T5-XXL, and an independent implementation reports 2x-2.5x on Chinchilla 70B.
facts.note: Speedup depends on acceptance rate and draft cost; it is not free for tiny target models.

facts.claim: Medusa adds multiple decoding heads and tree attention; Medusa-1 achieves >2.2x speedup without quality loss, and Medusa-2 reaches 2.3x-2.8x.
facts.note: Requires extra heads/training; verification is still needed.

facts.claim: EAGLE-2 achieves 3.05x-4.26x speedup, 20%-40% faster than EAGLE-1, with unchanged output distribution; EAGLE-3 reports up to 6.5x and about 1.4x over EAGLE-2.
facts.note: Large-model regimes; small-model gains are lower.

facts.claim: s1 uses 1,000 curated questions and 'budget forcing' to control thinking length; s1-32B reaches 56.7 AIME, 93.0 MATH and 59.6 GPQA in the reported table.
facts.note: 32B is not an SLM; this is evidence for test-time scaling, not for 1B models.

facts.claim: Compute-optimal test-time scaling can improve efficiency by more than 4x over a best-of-N baseline, and test-time compute can substitute for additional pretraining under a fixed FLOP budget.
facts.note: Effect varies strongly by prompt difficulty; easy prompts waste compute.

facts.claim: Minitron derives 8B and 4B models from a 15B model using depth/width/attention/MLP pruning plus distillation, requiring up to 40x fewer training tokens per model and <3% of the original training data.
facts.note: Structured pruning + retraining; not one-shot.

facts.claim: SparseGPT prunes 175B models to 50% sparsity in one shot with minimal loss, reaches 60% unstructured sparsity with negligible perplexity increase, and runs in under 4.5 hours on OPT-175B/BLOOM-176B.
facts.note: Unstructured sparsity rarely yields real speedups without hardware support.

facts.claim: Wanda prunes by weight magnitude times input activation, needs no retraining, and unstructured 50% sparse LLaMA-65B/LLaMA-2-70B matches dense zero-shot accuracy.
facts.note: Accuracy parity at 65B/70B does not mean latency gains.

facts.claim: AWQ finds that protecting only 1% of salient weight channels greatly reduces quantization error, and TinyChat delivers >3x speedup over FP16 on desktop and mobile GPUs.
facts.note: Speedup includes kernel fusion and platform-aware packing, not quantization alone.

facts.claim: GPTQ quantizes 175B models to 3-4 bits in about 4 GPU hours with negligible accuracy degradation.
facts.note: Post-training; calibration data matters.

facts.claim: NVIDIA's position paper argues SLMs are sufficient, more suitable and more economical for many repetitive agentic invocations; serving a 7B SLM is 10-30x cheaper than a 70-175B LLM in latency, energy and FLOPs.
facts.note: Position paper, not a controlled benchmark of all tasks.

facts.claim: Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2 is an 8.89B hybrid Mamba-Transformer, pruned and distilled from a 12B model, trained on ~10.6T tokens, supports 128K context, and achieves up to 6x higher throughput than similarly sized models while matching or beating Qwen3-8B on reasoning benchmarks.
facts.note: Vendor evaluation; hybrid architecture is the key mechanism.

facts.claim: MiniCPM's 1.2B and 2.4B non-embedding models are reported on par with 7B-13B LLMs; the work uses model wind-tunnel experiments and a Warmup-Stable-Decay scheduler.
facts.note: Benchmark-selective; not a general equivalence.

facts.claim: TinyLlama is 1.1B and trained on ~1T tokens for up to 3 epochs, outperforming OPT-1.3B and Pythia-1.4B on reported tasks.
facts.note: Shows data repetition can be useful, not that it is always safe.

facts.claim: Gemma 3 spans 1B-27B, adds vision, 128K+ context, uses distillation, and reduces KV-cache memory by interleaving local layers (1024-token span) with global layers.
facts.note: Gemma 3 4B-IT is reported competitive with Gemma 2 27B-IT.

facts.claim: Qwen3 spans 0.6B-235B, dense and MoE, integrates thinking and non-thinking modes, and reports Qwen3-1.7B/4B/8B/14B/32B comparable to Qwen2.5-3B/7B/14B/32B/72B respectively.
facts.note: Vendor benchmarks; the comparison is against the previous generation, not current same-size models.

facts.claim: Apple's 2025 on-device model is ~3B, uses KV-cache sharing and 2-bit quantization-aware training, and matches or surpasses comparably sized open baselines on public benchmarks and human evaluations.
facts.note: The interesting mechanism is system co-design, not a standalone model file.

facts.claim: Llama 3.2 1B/3B are structured-pruned from Llama 3.1 8B and distilled with logits from 8B and 70B teachers; they support 128K context; the 3B is reported to outperform Gemma 2 2.6B and Phi 3.5-mini on selected tasks.
facts.note: Selected tasks; vendor evaluation.

facts.claim: Gemma 3 270M has 270M total parameters, of which 170M are embeddings (256K vocab) and 100M are transformer blocks; it is INT4 QAT and used only 0.75% of a Pixel 9 Pro battery for 25 conversations in internal tests.
facts.note: A striking example of embedding-dominated small models.

facts.claim: Ternary Bonsai 2 2B is a 1.88B language model with ternary {-1,0,+1} weights, FP16 group scales (group 128), a fixed Walsh-Hadamard rotation, 24 blocks (18 linear-attention + 6 full-attention), 262K context, 248,320 vocab, and a 0.43GB PTQ1_0 file.
facts.note: Our binary parse confirms the metadata and tensor layout; quality claims remain vendor claims.

facts.claim: The Bonsai 2B PTQ1_0 file is 429,183,456 bytes and contains 320 tensors: 151 PTQ1_0 tensors (1,880,096,768 params) and 169 F32 tensors (1,728,320 params); tensor-only storage is 1.7778 bits/param and the whole file is 1.8245 bits/param.
facts.note: Calculated from the shipped GGUF v3 header and tensor table; includes metadata in the file-level number.

facts.claim: PTQ1_0 uses 28 bytes per 128 weights: 24 bytes of base-3 packed trits (5 per byte, first 120 values), 2 bytes of base-3 trits (4 per byte, last 8 values), and one FP16 scale. The encoder rescales base-3 codes q to ceil(q*256/243).
facts.note: Confirmed in the PrismML fork's ggml-common.h and ggml-quants.c; our Python decoder reproduces the integer path.

facts.claim: In the Bonsai 2B file, the token embedding is 508,559,360 parameters, 27.0% of the language model; FFN is 48.1%, full attention 20.7%, SSM/linear attention 4.1%.
facts.note: Parameter counts, not FLOPs; embedding lookup is memory-bound.

facts.claim: At 262,144 context, a full-attention-only FP16 KV cache for Bonsai 2B (24 layers, 2 KV heads, 256 key/value dim) would be 24.0GiB (25.8GB decimal) for one sequence; the hybrid 18-linear/6-full layout reduces it to 6.0GiB (6.4GB decimal). At 32K context it is 0.75GiB.
facts.note: Ignores allocator overhead, SSM state and KV quantization; runtimes typically use smaller contexts and/or quantized caches.

facts.claim: The shipped WebGPU bundle contains quantized matmul kernels for q4_0, q4_k, q8_0, iq, q6_k, q5_k, q3_k, q2_k and q1_0; a quantized KV-cache path with int8 key/value and scales; and a speculative-decoding interface whose default returns null for this model.
facts.value: many quant formats; int8 KV; specDecodeRunner -> null
facts.note: Static bundle analysis; runtime execution not observed.

facts.claim: The WebGPU bundle implements the Walsh-Hadamard transform in WGSL (hadamard-block-stages / column-butterfly) and reads Qwen3.5 hybrid-attention metadata such as full_attention_interval and layer_types.
facts.note: Static evidence that the rotation and hybrid layout are co-designed with the runtime.

facts.claim: Beyond Chinchilla-Optimal finds that for ~1B inference requests, models should be trained smaller and longer than Chinchilla-optimal; quality continued to improve up to 10,000 tokens/parameter in their experiments.
facts.note: Inference demand changes the optimal parameter/token tradeoff.

facts.claim: Scaling Laws for Precision finds that post-training quantization degradation increases as models are trained on more data, eventually making additional pretraining data actively harmful at fixed low precision.
facts.value: more data can hurt at fixed low precision
facts.note: A key limit on 'just add more data and quantize'.

facts.claim: The compute required to reach a fixed language-model performance threshold roughly halved every 8 months from 2012-2023 (95% CI 5-14 months), faster than Moore's law.
facts.note: Explains why new small models beat old big models.

facts.claim: MMLU-CF reports GPT-4o at 73.4% (5-shot) / 71.9% (0-shot) on its contamination-free test set, far below the ~88% often reported on MMLU; the benchmark uses a closed test set and decontamination rules.
facts.note: Not directly comparable to MMLU numbers due to different items/difficulty; illustrates benchmark inflation.

facts.claim: GSM1k, designed to mirror GSM8K, shows accuracy drops of up to 8% for leading models; a positive relationship (Spearman r^2=0.36) between GSM8K memorization and the GSM8K-GSM1k gap suggests partial contamination.
facts.note: Frontier models show smaller gaps; contamination is model- and family-dependent.

facts.claim: FrugalGPT's cascade can match GPT-4's performance with up to 98% cost reduction, or improve accuracy by 4% at the same cost, by routing queries among cheaper and stronger models.
facts.note: Cost depends on API prices at the time; routing errors can hurt.

facts.claim: RouteLLM reports over 2x cost reduction in some cases without compromising response quality by routing between a strong and a weak model.
facts.note: Router quality and distribution shift are the bottlenecks.

facts.claim: Across 67 frontier models, multi-model routing/voting gains are capped by the all-models-wrong rate beta; on open-ended math beta was 0.052, and on execution-graded code 0.079, so ensembles rarely beat the single best model without a strong query-level routing signal.
facts.note: A caution against 'just ensemble small models'.

facts.claim: Long-CoT SFT can degrade SLMs (<=3B): in some settings, training on only 8K long-CoT examples loses up to 75% of prior performance, and even 220K examples fail to recover for some very small models.
facts.note: Error accumulation; more reasoning tokens are not automatically better.

facts.claim: Interleaved-Policy Distillation improves Qwen3-0.6B/s1K from 24.55 to 29.72 on a seven-benchmark average by generating traces the student can actually reach, rather than filtering or masking losses.
facts.note: Small-model-specific post-training; not a general scaling result.

facts.claim: SimpleQA is designed to test short-form factuality and 'know what you know'; in Phi-4's table, phi-4 scores 3.0 versus GPT-4o's 39.4, showing a large long-tail factual gap.
facts.note: Small models can be competitive on reasoning benchmarks while failing factual recall.

facts.claim: Embers of Autoregression predicts LLMs are more accurate when the task, target output and input are high-probability under the training distribution; accuracy degrades on low-probability variants even when the task is deterministic.
facts.note: A mechanistic reason small models fail on rare facts/edge cases.

facts.claim: RAG combines parametric and non-parametric memory and improves knowledge-intensive tasks; Self-RAG adds adaptive retrieval and self-critique.
facts.note: Retrieval quality and latency dominate; RAG does not fix reasoning.

facts.claim: Qwen3.5-2B uses a 6 x (3 x Gated DeltaNet + 1 x Gated Attention) layout, 24 layers, hidden 2048, 248,320 vocab (tied LM head), 8 Q / 2 KV heads, head dim 256, 262,144 context, and MTP training.
facts.note: Bonsai's architecture is unchanged from this base.

facts.claim: Tokenizer fertility on our Japanese test sentence: Qwen3.5-2B 31 tokens, Gemma 3 270M 33, Qwen3-0.6B 36, SmolLM3 43, Llama 3.2 1B 44, Phi-4-mini 45, TinyLlama 70 (2.26x Qwen3.5).
facts.value: 31 vs 70 tokens for the same sentence
facts.note: One sentence is not a full fertility study; it illustrates the mechanism. Token counts include BOS for some tokenizers.

facts.claim: Embedding share of parameters: Gemma 3 270M 62.1%, Qwen3.5-2B 27.0%, Qwen3-0.6B 25.9%, Llama 3.2 1B 21.2%, BitNet 2B4T 16.4%, Phi-4-mini 16.2%, SmolLM3 8.8%, TinyLlama 6.0%.
facts.note: Approximate totals; exact counts depend on tied embeddings, vision towers and padding.

facts.claim: Ternary Bonsai 2 27B reports 98.2% intelligence retained at ~9.1x smaller and 46.8 tok/s on a laptop; the 8B reports 75.5 average at 1.75GB and 27 tok/s on an iPhone.
facts.note: Vendor benchmarks; not independently replicated.

facts.claim: Bonsai's 2B card says speculative decoding with a draft model was slower than plain decoding on everyday prompts at 2B, so the 2B ships without a draft model and uses prompt lookup alone; the 4B/9B add MTP/DFlash drafters on copy-heavy prompts, with 1.7x-1.8x on M5 Pro and up to 3.9x on iPhone.
facts.note: Confirms that speculative decoding is not a universal win at small target sizes.

facts.claim: The Bonsai 2B model card lists a 0.43GB PTQ1_0 language file, a 0.36GB Q8_0 vision projector and a 0.67GB BF16 projector; the headline 0.43GB is language-only.
facts.note: Deployment footprint is larger than the headline number when vision is enabled.

facts.claim: The PrismML fork's PTQ1_0 dequantizer uses the integer identity ((byte * 3^n mod 256) * 3) >> 8, which recovers the base-3 trit without floating point.
facts.note: Our decoder reproduces the same 128 values; see rea/evidence/ptq1_block.md.
